trust_decision.summary: Whether bytes from an untrusted container may be materialised into memory or onto disk is decided by comparing a declared entry size against a fixed byte cap before inflation: 256 KiB for ISDOCX document/manifest entries (src/X/Reader.php::readEntry) and 32 MiB for a single attachment (each Supplement::getContents()/getStream()/saveTo()); no such decision exists on the PDF path, where the pdfparser object is inflated before any cap is applied.

landing_point.why: The summary names a decompression bomb in an ISDOCX/PDF container, so the first place an engineer greps is the attachment extraction that calls ZipArchive::getFromName() with no size check; the same file's getStream() (src/X/Supplement.php:51) and saveTo() (src/X/Supplement.php:64) are the neighbouring sinks.

fix_sites.module_kind: container reader (ISDOCX/ZIP) - document and manifest entry inflation

fix_sites.entry_point: Invoice\Supplement::getContents() / saveTo() on a local-path supplement
PDF\Supplement::getContents() / saveTo() on a PDF embedded file
fix_sites.module_kind: attachment object (PDF embedded file) - second implementation

fix_sites.entry_point: (internal helper) X\Zip::entrySize() used by X\Reader::readEntry and X\Supplement::checkSize

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The PDF side is third-party territory: smalot/pdfparser's PDFObject::getContent() owns decompression and has already materialised the bytes, so a cap applied after it returns bounds what we hand out and the reader's own getContent() call needs no pre-check.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimately large attachments must keep working: this library's own PDF writer embeds supplements up to 16 MiB and the ISDOCX writer embeds any path with no cap, so an over-broad fix that reuses the 256 KiB document cap (or applies a cap to every embedded file in PDF\Reader) breaks round-tripping of attachments between 256 KiB and 16 MiB; the pinned tests also read attachments back with a plain getContents()/->contents and no limit.

O6_input_shapes: container: ISDOCX/ZIP document entry named by manifest.xml, .isdoc entry found by extension scan, and attachment entries; PDF embedded-file streams
access path: $supplement->contents / ->stream / ->ok properties, getContents(), getStream(), saveTo(), isOk()
limit argument: omitted (32 MiB default), explicit integer (tighter or wider), null (cap disabled)
entry-name resolution: case-insensitive attachment filename (findRealFile) vs exact 'manifest.xml' vs manifest-declared main filename
size source: declared central-directory size (pre-inflation) plus a running byte budget on the inflated stream (saveTo) and a post-decompression strlen (PDF)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PDF read inflates every /EmbeddedFile with $object->getContent() for XML sniffing (and before the supplement is even constructed), with no declared-Length cap; the 1.x fix added no pre-check in PDF\Reader at all.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The third-party parser already decompressed the stream - bounding it is not this project's code, so the reader only needs to sniff it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (src/PDF) from the src/X landing point, reached through the same public Reader::file() call

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PDF\Supplement computes sha1 over the full embedded file in its constructor (via the SmartObject $this->contents -> getContents()), so the bomb is inflated during Reader::file(), before any caller can pass a size limit; the fix's cap in getContents() fires only after getContent() has already returned the whole payload.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A digest must cover the whole file by design, and the bytes were already materialised by the PDF library, so the cap on the return value is as far as this layer can go.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same src/PDF package as the reader route but a second file that has to be changed independently

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a byte-budget guard on getContents()/getStream() (not only on saveTo) so a forged under-reported central-directory size cannot inflate past the cap
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix's own saveTo() adds exactly this running budget with the comment that statName() may under-report (fix.diff:1534-1536), so a maintainer would plausibly have put the same guard on the in-memory read paths

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a size limit threaded through checkSupplementDigest(), the shared sink behind $supplement->ok / isOk() on all three implementations
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every implementation's ok/isOk() funnels through this one helper that calls getContents() with no limit, so a maintainer could have capped the digest path itself instead of per-implementation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an attachment size guard on the ISDOCX write path, mirroring the PDF writer's existing 16 MiB check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the PDF writer already refuses supplements over 1<<24 bytes, so symmetry makes the same guard in X\Writer a natural maintainer edit

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a cap on the plain-.isdoc file_get_contents() read
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer hardening 'reading untrusted files' may add the cap at the top-level reader; it is the same read-into-memory sink and the report does not distinguish container rows

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a size guard in fromPath()/fromString(), i.e. refusing to construct a supplement whose local file is over the default cap
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the local supplement is the write-side twin of the read-side cap and already computes sha1 over the whole file at construction

O9_family: uncontrolled resource consumption - decompression bomb / declared-size amplification (CWE-400, CWE-409)
